blocks.text: For software that needs safety and quality `gg` offers extra checks:

code: gg check --profile safety main.gg   # also rejects unsafe, panic, recursion, heap use,
gg test --coverage                  # statement, decision, condition and MC/DC coverage
gg coverage --annotate              # list what never ran
gg fuzz main.gg                     # run fn fuzz_target(data: []u8) on mutated inputs
gg sbom main.gg                     # software bill of materials (CycloneDX or SPDX)
gg repro main.gg                    # build twice, compare the bytes (reproducible build)
gg unsafe-audit main.gg             # every unsafe block, asm, foreign function and static

blocks.text: To inspect the compiler stages there are `gg emit-ll` (LLVM IR), `gg emit-bc` (bitcode), `gg ast` (the syntax tree) and `gg attrs` (uses of `@attributes`, as JSON).

**Editor:** the Greengold VS Code extension, with the built-in language server (LSP), shows errors as you type, go to definition (`F12`), documentation on hover, completion after `.`, formatting with `Shift+Alt+F`, the compiler's fixes in the lightbulb menu and Run/Release/Build buttons. Saving the file also applies the `safe` fixes.

blocks.q: Which command lists every `unsafe` block of a program?
blocks.why: `unsafe-audit` collects the places where you must ensure memory safety by hand.

options: Things like `unsafe`, `panic`, recursion and heap use
blocks.why: The safety profile switches off features that are hard to prove safe.
